roster.name: Worker
roster.desc: Gathers food, wood, stone and gold, and builds

roster.name: Spear
roster.desc: Beats mounted units and beasts; weak to ranged and infantry

roster.name: Skirmisher
roster.desc: Beats archers and war beasts; weak to infantry and mounted

roster.name: Archer
roster.desc: Beats infantry; weak to skirmishers and mounted

roster.name: Healer
roster.desc: Heals wounded friends nearby; never fights. Weak to scouts and raiders

roster.name: Swordsman
roster.desc: Beats buildings, spears and skirmishers; weak to archers

roster.name: Mounted Archer
roster.desc: A bow on horseback: beats infantry and slow units; weak to skirmishers, spears and cavalry

roster.name: Scout
roster.desc: Fast, light and far-sighted: finds the enemy, catches skirmishers, engines, healers and workers; weak in a real fight, spears beat it

roster.name: War Beast
roster.desc: A great beast with riders: slow and very tough, beats buildings and foot soldiers; spears, skirmishers and bolt throwers bring it down

roster.name: Catapult
roster.desc: Beats massed units (splash); weak to mounted

roster.name: Bolt Thrower
roster.desc: Beats lines of infantry; weak to mounted

roster.name: Siege Tower
roster.desc: Pushed up to an enemy wall, it lets your foot soldiers onto the wall walk; doesn't fight

roster.name: Unique Unit
roster.desc: The race's signature (data/uniques.json): the theme the prompt asked for, else its creature's or culture's; a bigger budget

roster._status_note: parked (Dominic, 2026-10-13: "remove the sapper unit, not needed"); the blast code in combat.gd and its test stay for later
roster.name: Sapper
roster.desc: Walks up to a building and blows it up, and itself with it: a wall or gate tile outright, a house at once, a Town Center in three. Weak to everything that fights

roster.name: Great Sling
roster.desc: Hits buildings from far away (12 tiles); stops and unpacks before it shoots, packs up before it moves. Weak to cavalry

roster.name: Trade Cart
roster.desc: Carries goods from your Market to another of yours or an ally's and brings gold back: the further apart, the more a trip pays. Never fights

_roster_doc: each slot is a unit line: its first age (`tier`), the building that trains it, its name on the tech tree page, and `last_age` when it stops before the last age. Slots with "status": "planned" are only on the page: the generator skips them (milestone 12). `upgrades`: false keeps the first unit for every later age (no second tier: the healer). `own_seed`: the line draws from its own random stream (prompt + slot), so adding it leaves every other line's recipes as they were. `engine`: a siege line: its body is the engine of that name in the race's take (families.json `siege`, a creature's own `siege` first), crewed by the race's workers. `bonus`: attack bonus by class that the line gets whatever it holds (the swordsman's counters: spears, skirmishers, buildings; pricing.gd), and `price_points`: what that bonus adds to the line's price points. `mount`: the line rides the race's mount ("always": a race with nothing to ride lacks the line; "prefer": it goes on foot), `unless_mounted`: the race lacks the line when that other line already rides (a centaur's archers are mounted archers), `stats` (hp, attack, speed, range, sight in tiles, armour) added to the line whatever it holds, `stats_on_foot` on top for one with no mount; `budget_add`: points over the age's budget (the unique unit), `noun`: the line's own name over its weapon's (the Scout), `needs_hands`: a creature with a harness for hands (creatures.json) lacks the line, `armed`: false: an engine line with no weapon part (the trade cart), `take`: the creature's (else its culture's) field naming the engine's take, `siege` by default (the war beast: `war_beast`, creatures.json / families.json: elephant, boar, tarantula, heron, mantis), `crew`: the line whose unit (at the engine's first age) crews it, the worker by default (the war beast's riders: the spear line, D-129), `crew_drop`: the crew's part slots left off (riders stow wings, capes and banners)

cost.roles_note: a role's own price terms (pricing.gd): pct of the base price (soldiers went from base 60 to 100, about 1.7x, D-125; siege engines kept at 60%), then the total is at least floor and at most ceiling (before the creature's cost_pct: workers 50-75 food, a centaur's the dearest, D-078), pop sets the role's population (workers 1, even on a horse's body), and mix replaces the parts' cost_mix

trade.note: trade carts (src/sim/trade.gd): a cart takes goods from its home Market to another (yours or an ally's, at least min_tiles apart, centre to centre) and brings back d * d / sq_div + d * lin_pct / 100 gold a round trip, d the tiles between them (genre trade: the gold per trip grows faster than the distance); paid on arrival home, lost with the cart

combat.shot_note: shots fly (combat.gd, shots.gd): milli-tiles a tick, shot_speed for bows, shot_speeds by the weapon's first tag that has one. A shot flies at the spot its target stands on, led by shot_lead_pct of the way it walks during the flight, and hits its target if its body still covers that spot (within shot_slack) when it lands, else the ground; with shot_strays 1 a miss may hit another foe of the shooter on the spot (off: shooting into a charging crowd then wastes shots, and massed archers no longer beat a mixed army at equal cost; tests/mass_battle.gd). Shooters fighting on their own skip a foe the shots in the air will kill.
combat.stance_note: stances (combat.gd): defensive units engage foes within defend_sight (or their reach, if longer) and give up once leash from where they stood, then walk back (leash stays above defend_sight, or they would turn back short of a foe that stands still).
combat.note: ticks at 20 Hz; distances in milli-tiles. Damage = max(min_damage, sum over attack classes the target has of max(0, attack - armour)).
combat.heal_note: healers (heal.gd): each one heals the most wounded unit of its own team (not itself, not animals, not buildings) within heal_sight, walking up to heal_range (edge to edge) when idle: heal_amount hp (x the unit's heal stat) every heal_reload ticks
combat.splash_note: splash (catapults, combat.gd): a shot whose weapon has `splash` (milli-tiles) lands on its spot and hurts every unit within it (and enemy buildings), less further out: damage x (splash - gap) / splash, gap from the spot to the body's edge; its target takes it in full if still there, a building always. Friends in the area take splash_friend_pct of it (the genre's stone throwers hurt their own side too). `min_range` (tiles): it can't hit what is closer, and steps back from a foe that comes in. `pass` (milli-tiles, bolt throwers): the shot also hits every foe whose body is on its last `pass` of flight. `reload` (ticks) on a weapon overrides melee_reload / ranged_reload. `targets: buildings` (rams, the great sling, the sapper): goes for buildings only. `unpack` / `pack` (ticks, the great sling): it stands that long before its first shot, and packs up that long before it can move (world.gd _pack). `blast` (milli-tiles, the sapper): its blow blows it up, hurting everything within (less further out, friends at splash_friend_pct), a wall, palisade or gate under it losing `blast_line_pct` of its hit points.

movement.note: Movement classes (sim_map.gd CLASSES): a unit takes the first class whose tag it has, else ground. Terrains list which classes cross them (terrain.json move).

wonder.note: Wonder victory (src/sim/match.gd): a player whose Wonder is finished and stands for hold_seconds wins for their team; victory false turns it off (the Wonder is then just a monument)

fog.note: sight radii in tiles; the fog grid updates every `every` ticks (5 Hz)

trails.note: worn trails (src/sim/trails.gd, milestone 15): every `every` ticks each walking (not flying) unit wears its cell by `add` (up to `max`); every `decay_every` ticks every cell grows back by `decay`. A cell worn to `trail` is a trail: the view draws it, and walkers on it are `speed_pct` faster (0: off; the experiment in docs/milestones/m15-maps.md)

high_ground.note: high ground (src/sim/sim_map.gd heights, milestone 15): a shooter a level above its target reaches `reach` milli-tiles further, one below reaches that much less and deals `uphill_damage_pct` of its damage (arrows fall short; integers, no dice). Units see `sight_unit` tiles further per level they stand on, buildings `sight_building`. Ground above the viewer's level blocks sight past its rim (fog.gd).
